name: Remove One Element
description: You are given an array $$$a$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ integers. You can remove at most one element from this array. Thus, the final length of the array is $$$n-1$$$ or $$$n$$$. Your task is to calculate the maximum possible length of the strictly increasing contiguous subarray of the remaining array. Recall that the contiguous subarray $$$a$$$ with indices from $$$l$$$ to $$$r$$$ is $$$a[l \dots r] = a_l, a_{l + 1}, \dots, a_r$$$. The subarray $$$a[l \dots r]$$$ is called strictly increasing if $$$a_l \lt a_{l+1} \lt \dots \lt a_r$$$.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of elements in $$$a$$$. The second line of the input contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$), where $$$a_i$$$ is the $$$i$$$-th element of $$$a$$$.
output_specification: Print one integer — the maximum possible length of the strictly increasing contiguous subarray of the array $$$a$$$ after removing at most one element.
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
